summary:
Our project addresses the problem of comparing locations on Earth with conditions similar to those on Mars and the Moon for the purpose of establishing landing sites.
Our website contains a catalog of locations on our planet that may have conditions similar to those on other celestial bodies, which are more extreme and not common on Earth. These locations are compared to conditions on other planets, allowing for compatibility checks.
This website is very clear, easy to use, and very intuitive, making it very easy for a wider audience, from laypeople to scientists, to use.
Our project already has the data compared in one place, which will significantly simplify navigation between data and actual locations, significantly automating work in this area.
details:
TerraTwin Lite is a web application that helps users explore potential Earth analogs for selected regions of Mars by comparing terrain characteristics derived from real elevation data.

Users can choose between Gale, Jezero, and Elysium / InSight and examine three terrestrial study areas: Atacama, Mojave, and Puna. The application displays their locations, terrain features, data sources, and processing limitations. Users can select up to two Earth candidates and compare them with the selected Mars reference.

Our Python pipeline processes predefined 50 × 50 km windows using the USGS HRSC + MOLA blended elevation model for Mars and NASADEM for Earth. It prepares local metric grids, handles missing data, and calculates two terrain descriptors: median slope and elevation relief, defined as the difference between the 90th and 10th elevation percentiles. A TypeScript backend serves the prepared catalogs and comparison results. The interface uses React, TypeScript, Vite, and Leaflet, with deployment on Vercel.

The project makes an initial terrain comparison easier to inspect and explain. Instead of presenting an unexplained similarity score, it shows the underlying measurements, signed differences, units, sources, and limitations. This could support early discussions about terrestrial environments for planetary field research and equipment testing.

Our creative approach combines planetary and terrestrial elevation products in a single, transparent comparison workflow. We also investigated how grid spacing, the area evaluated, derivative distance, and smoothing affect calculated slopes. These experiments helped us distinguish a working software demonstration from a scientifically validated ranking.

Our team considered differences in planetary coordinate systems, spatial resolution, data quality, missing values, and the interpretation of terrain similarity. The current version uses a small, predefined catalog rather than searching the entire Earth. Experimental similarity scoring remains disabled because a shared effective analysis scale, weights, and tolerances have not yet been justified. TerraTwin Lite compares selected topographic properties; it does not reproduce Martian environmental conditions or assess mission safety.

The result is a working, browser-based prototype with traceable data and an accessible comparison interface for desktop and mobile screens.

Live application: https://ttlite.vercel.app
